findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "rzlt_overview" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: What RZLT (rzlt.io) is and sells: an AI-native growth and marketing agency for technology companies. Returns the four core services with links, how RZLT deliver…

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "send_message" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Sends a message to RZLT's team for the person you are helping; the team replies by email within one working day. Use it when the person wants RZLT to get back t…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_rzlt, send_message · Private data: rzlt_overview, check_ai_readiness · Public sink: send_message · Destructive: rzlt_overview.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_rzlt, send_message · Private data: rzlt_overview, check_ai_readiness · Public sink: send_message · Destructive: rzlt_overview

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
